thread:
Ravi Kumar: Quick update: burst-smoothing-v3 canary finished. This combines adaptive kv-prefetch smoothing + microbatch elasticity. Results: p50 -1%, p95 -10%, p99 -26% on convo-heavy traces. Token-cost -7% overall. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/bench/2098765432
Tess Alvarez: awesome. which models benefit most?
Ravi Kumar: long-context customers (avg seq >500) and models with large KV caches. Short RPCs unchanged.
BenchBot: test harness: 48h trace replay + 2x synthetic burst. Details on dash link.
Tess Alvarez: config used?
Ravi Kumar: snippet used in canary:
```
burst_smoothing_v3:
  kv_prefetch_ms: 180
  smoothing_window: 300
  microbatch_min: 2
  microbatch_max: 16
  elasticity_factor: 1.25
```
Ravi Kumar: note: we saw a tiny p50 regression (+3ms) for ultra-short requests (<10 tokens) in the synthetic microbench.
Tess Alvarez: probable cause: microbatch_min=2 introduces one extra scheduling hop. Can we add a fast-path?
Ravi Kumar: agreed. we'll gate microbatch_min on model tag 'tiny' and keep fast-path off during canary.
infra-bot: Canary deploy 2098765432 -> started at 2098765437, rollout=5%
sre-bot: Snapshot +45m: p99 -24% vs baseline, cost -6.9%, host-cpu +1.5% on canary nodes. No error uptick. Link: https://sre.redwood.internal/snapshots/2098765432-45m
Docs: I'll draft internal note describing the knobs and recommended defaults for chat vs rpc.
Ravi Kumar: rollback triggers: auto-rollback if p99 increases >6% for 5m or error-rate +0.6% abs. Manual rollback commands in runbook.
Tess Alvarez: plan: hold at 5% for 1h, then 25% after sanity checks, enable tiny fast-path, then finish rollout to 100% if stable over 6h. I'll post status updates here.
Ravi Kumar: TL;DR: burst-smoothing-v3 cuts p99 ~26% for long-chat workloads and saves ~7% token-cost. Canary rolling, monitoring 72h. :rocket:
